title: Use AIDA as a Message Clarity Checklist
subtitle: Make the message relevant, understandable, honest, and actionable.
description: Check whether a message earns attention, makes the relevant point understandable, explains why it matters, and gives the reader a clear next action without treating AIDA as a persuasion guarantee.

lifeOsSource.hack: Use Attention, Interest, Desire, and Action as four editing questions, not as a promise that a message will persuade.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Name the audience and desired next step, review the opening for relevance, remove information that does not help understanding, explain the concrete value or consequence honestly, and end with one clear action the reader can accept, decline, or ignore.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Can the reader quickly tell why this matters, what is being asked, and what they should do next without exaggerated claims or hidden pressure?

faq.question: What matters more than a clever hook?
faq.answer: Relevance. The opening should help the intended reader recognize the problem, decision, or value without hiding the point behind theatrics.
faq.answerHtml: Relevance. The opening should help the intended reader recognize the problem, decision, or value without hiding the point behind theatrics.

intro.html: AIDA can be used as four editing questions rather than a sales formula. The goal is not to force persuasion. It is to make the message easier to recognize, understand, evaluate, and act on.

sections.title: 1. Attention and interest: relevance first
sections.html: Start with the reader's actual problem, context, decision, or desired result. Give only the context needed to understand the proposal and prefer concrete language over generic hooks.

sections.title: 2. Desire: explain value without overclaiming
sections.html: Describe the plausible benefit, avoided cost, or consequence and the conditions attached to it. Do not invent proof, testimonials, scarcity, or certain outcomes.

sections.title: 3. Action: ask for one clear next step
sections.html: State what the reader can do next and what commitment it implies. Keep the action proportional to the information available and make refusal or deferral possible when appropriate.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace unsupported response-rate improvements, fabricated A/B outcomes, and formula-like persuasion claims with a bounded editing checklist.
